item.title: Daring to Democratize Mobility: Conversion and Socialization in the Automotive Industry · BG | berlinergazette.de
item.description: Radical movements are calling for changes in mobility and traffic. They urge car-centric societies to reconsider current mobility behaviors, car production, and car usage in light of the structural conditions of industrial-fossil capitalism. This includes making mobility needs, infrastructure design, production, and mobility services the subject of democratic negotiation. item.title: Retail for ‘the People’: Department Stores in Socialist Yugoslavia · BG | berlinergazette.de
item.description: The decline of department stores is part of a broader process of capitalist restructuring, most visibly exemplified by the proliferation of suburban shopping malls and digital commerce. The loss of local department stores in the city often affects residents because department stores were built with the community’s needs in mind when city centers were designed to be more human-oriented. Ivana Mihaela Žimbrek focuses on department stores in socialist Yugoslavia and their legacy.

item.title: Realizing Democracy: Why We Need to Switch Off the Autopilot and Take Control · BG | berlinergazette.de
item.description: We must defend democracy, not as it currently exists, but by making it a reality. As long as the economy remains outside the realm of democratic control, democracy is intertwined with a destructive, colonial economic system that threatens our existence on this planet. In his contribution to the “Deep Democracy” series, Lukas Warning argues, that no socio-ecological transformation can occur unless the restructuring of the economy is subject to collective control. item.title: Davos and Doom: The Green Opium of the Progressed and Its Sacrifice Zones · BG | berlinergazette.de
item.description: The old sovereignty argument led us to believe that food, water, and land would belong to the people again. This argument ignored the fact that capitalist restructuring in the name of sovereignty always meant more wealth for the same people. Nevertheless, new sovereignists are repeating this mantra. However, a new vision of sovereignty is emerging from those who have been reduced to colonies, such as ecological sovereignty. Irina Velicu dares to connect the dots.

item.title: Feminist Housing Policy: Socializing Living Space, Democratizing Care · BG | berlinergazette.de
item.description: Feminist housing policy, including the demand for socialization, should not be viewed as an additional adjustment to existing housing policy instruments. Rather, it strives for a structural transformation of social reproduction relations. item.title: From the Ruins of Democracy as We Know It: In Defense of Autonomy · BG | berlinergazette.de
item.description: A thorough critique of liberal democracy reveals an alternative reality of democracy obscured by the myths and institutions of colonial capitalist modernity. It also illuminates why autonomy must play a central role in any emancipatory, collective endeavor. How we can organize and navigate a transition out of our current predicament? Which existing structures could be useful? And how? In his contribution to the “Deep Democracy” series, Carlos Tornel identifies ‘choke points’ for intervention.

item.title: Tech-Solutionism and Heatwaves: Promoting Air Conditioning Distracts From Systemic Change · BG | berlinergazette.de
item.description: It’s a vicious cycle. The warmer the planet becomes, the greater the demand for cooling technologies. These technologies have an ecological footprint in terms of resource consumption and production cycles that exacerbates the ecological crisis. According to Rose Wanjiku, this demonstrates that there is no one-size-fits-all solution. item.title: Mainstreaming the Far Right, Entrenching Neoliberalism: Italy’s Political Laboratory From Berlusconi to Meloni · BG | berlinergazette.de
item.description: Giorgia Meloni’s cabinet is now one of the most stable governments in the history of the Italian Republic. This seems to disprove the widespread warnings of an impending decline in democracy that accompanied Meloni’s election in 2022. However, considering the aftermath of Berlusconism, the situation in Italy is more subtle – and perhaps more disturbing – than expected. According to Daniela Caterina, Adriano Cozzolino, Gemma Gasseau, and Davide Monaco, the situation offers a sobering lesson for t

item.title: The Lost Art of Making a Revolution: Why Are Radical Political Protests Followed by Bitter Disillusionment? · BG | berlinergazette.de
item.description: In recent years, every enthusiastic mass mobilization has inevitably been followed by bitter disillusionment. However, the improvement of repressive techniques and the overwhelming legacy of structures of domination are not the only reasons for this phenomenon. Slave Cubela argues that in an age when people can be mobilized for mass protests at the push of a button, we no longer engage deeply enough with the art of revolution.

item.title: Who Decides? How to Transform Society Through Self-Management · BG | berlinergazette.de
item.description: Deepening democracy means answering an elementary question: Who decides the conditions of our shared life? The notion of self-management asserts that those who produce and maintain society should collectively determine its direction. In their contribution to the “Deep Democracy” series, Jörg Nowak and Gabriel Teles explore self-management as the core of a radical transformation of society.

item.title: The Canton of Cartagena: A Forgotten Experiment in Municipal Democracy Without Borders · BG | berlinergazette.de
item.description: The famous Paris Commune had a little sister: the Canton of Cartagena. Its neglected history is linked to both the federalist revolution in Spain in 1873 and the colonial and global social protests of that time. In her contribution to the “Deep Democracy” series, Jeanne Moisand explores this inspiring case.

item.title: They Can’t Represent Us! How to Cross Out Revenge and Highlight Justice · BG | berlinergazette.de
item.description: When your whole world feels like a dull shadow of what it once was, an undercurrent of menace and sadness leaves you with a sense of dread. Rage builds up, filling you with a frenzy to act or sending you into a deep reverie of sorrow. What if it does all of that at once? A poetic exercise by Eliana Otta.

item.title: Infrastructural Violence: Who Dares to Disrupt the Flow of Goods and Energy? · BG | berlinergazette.de
item.description: Governments across the Americas are expanding their military capabilities to secure capital accumulation and infrastructure development. Despite the violence, people continue to defend captured territories in order to protect their communities and the environment. Alke Jenss examines the case of Mexico.

item.title: Calculating ‘War-Readiness’: The Militarization of Healthcare Between Affirmation and Resistance · BG | berlinergazette.de
item.description: The militarization of society has not spared the healthcare system. Hospitals and medical staff are being made ‘fit for war.’ This regressive social transformation, driven by the war effort, is met with both support and resistance within the healthcare sector. Nadja Rakowitz assesses the situation.
